Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business) and
Item Number you are commenting on. The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the
three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.
Example: PUBLIC COMMENT: New Business Item A
Watch the Meeting Online
Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link:
City Council Meeting Videos
Spectrum cable: Live streaming on Channel 3, Public Access Channel.
   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, February 16, 2021

    CALL TO ORDER
    PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Liao
    ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  2. PRESENTATION

  A. PROCLAMATION RECOGNIZING FEBRUARY AS BLACK HISTORY MONTH
  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 2, 2021.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 2, 2021.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 16, 2021  2
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JANUARY 2021

  This is the presentation of City investments for the month of January 2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for January 2021 in conformance with the City’s adopted
  2020-21 Investment Policy.

  D. FRAUD, WASTE AND ABUSE HOTLINE

  In an effort to continuously update the City’s Administrative Policies, the City
  Manager has worked with the City Attorney’s Office to update Administrative
  Policy #505, “Fraud Waste, and Abuse in the Workplace.” As part of this effort,
  Section 2.4 calls out the creation of a Fraud Hotline. The number designated
  for the hotline is (626) 308-2807 and will be launched upon City Council’s
  approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the creation of a Fraud,
  Waste, and Abuse hotline.

  E. CITY OF SAN GABRIEL LEGISLATIVE PLATFORM 2021 FINAL DRAFT

  On February 2, 2021, staff introduced the City of San Gabriel Legislative
  Platform to the City Council to outline the City’s position on legislative,
  regulatory or policy issues that impact or affect the City. The Platform was
  created to provide Council and staff with the direction to support or oppose
  legislation, after Council Consideration. After Council’s review and feedback,
  staff was directed to bring the Platform before the Council again for a final
  draft to include the City Council’s suggestions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the final draft of the City of San
  Gabriel Legislative Platform 2021.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 16, 2021  3
   6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH FIRST TRANSIT FOR DIAL-A-RIDE SERVICE

  The City of San Gabriel provides Dial-A-Ride service for City residents age 62
  and over and individuals with disabilities. The City contracts with a transit
  provider, First Transit, to manage and operate the Dial-A-Ride service. At the
  February 2, 2021 regular meeting, the City Council reviewed the program
  information and requested that staff return with an extension of the contract
  with First Transit to allow staff time to review and provide transit options for
  Council’s consideration. The amendment to the Dial-A-Ride Transportation
  Services Agreement can be extended for an additional period of up to six
  months, if necessary. The rate for this extension is $37,500 per month. This
  program is funded through Proposition A Local Return funds.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Amendment to Dial-A-
  Ride Transportation Services Agreement with First Transit and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the documents.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MID-YEAR BUDGET UPDATE

  The mid-year budget report examines the financial results of the General
  Fund through January 31, 2021. The financial information is synthesized, and
  updated budget projections for both revenues and expenditures are
  developed for the remainder of the fiscal year.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council receive and file the report.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 16, 2021  4
   Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 2, 2021, at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

 Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at

 Persons with Disabilities. Upon request, this Agenda will be made available in

 Persons requesting a Translator. Any person requesting translation for the meeting
 must notify the City Clerk’s Department at cityclerk@sgch.org at least 48 hours before
 the meeting.
 Questions about this Agenda? Should any person have a question concerning any of
 the above Agenda items prior to the meeting, please contact the City Clerk at
 cityclerk@sgch.org during regular office hours.

 Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to
 participate in a meeting should direct such a request to the City Clerk Department by
 emailing cityclerk@sgch.org at least 48 hours before the meeting, if possible.

MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 16, 2021
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  5:32 P.M. on Tuesday, February 16, 2021, with all Council Members and staff participating
  by teleconference.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Armine
  Chaparyan; Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen, Chief
  City Clerk Sharon Clark, and Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck.

I  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

  1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Norma Davalos provided comments in favor of small houses for sale rather than
  apartments for rent for an affordable housing project at 405 S. Del Mar Avenue.

  2. STUDY SESSION

  A. 405 SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE HOUSING OPTIONS

  The presentation was made by City Manager Lazzaretto, Economic Development
  Manager Domenica Megerdichian, and Related Companies development team
  representatives Meea Kang, Rose Olson, and Jennifer lng-aram.

  Discussion included unit sizes; parking space allotment; site challenges that limit

I  project components; tax credit program in relation to type of units; wrap-around
  services; pros and cons of types of units; elevator inclusion for three stories or
  seniors; underground parking being cost-prohibitive; mixing or separating family
  and senior units; benefits of apartment units rather than homes for sale; partnering
  with community organizations for services; and community outreach messaging.

  3. ADJOURNMENT

  The City Council meeting was adjourned at 6:44 P.M.
